limits: The first GUI repair completed routing and setup/hold checks but retained 445 extracted max_ss slew violations, 0 capacitance and 0 fanout violations. Its failed evidence remains preserved and is not adopted.

Five worst data-distribution driver instances were absent before the first post-GRT design repair and appeared as clkdlybuf4s25_1 after it. This version changes standard new-optimization cell selection; it does not claim a fully established internal resizer defect or predict success.

The standard EXTRA_EXCLUDED_CELLS wildcard prevents new clkdlybuf-family selections during optimization. It does not remove existing instances, omit timing models, waive violations or modify the saved RTL/netlist as text.

The exact first-repair global-route checkpoint reuses its mapping, placement and improved clock tree before the weak-buffer insertion stage. Standard design repair, all-nine-corner timing repair, detailed routing, extraction and stream-out execute again.

The original 50 ns GUI clock, final base SDC, fanout limit 10, 0.75 ns slew limit, capacitance constraints and all nine signoff corners remain unchanged. New full extracted setup/hold/electrical checks are mandatory.
Every changed layout requires new S12 DRC, S13 LVS and S14 routed-functional/extracted-STA evidence. Finite verification is not dynamic SDF verification, formal equivalence or fabrication readiness.
The source is bound by its immutable execution hash and current raw self-checksum. Later ordinary review metadata may change its full raw record hash without changing the executed source.
